analysis.overall: You spent 77% of the day in range with a strong morning baseline, though late carb absorption after dinner and breakfast caused extended high peaks that took repeated corrections to resolve.

events.title: Post-lunch elevation
events.description: After a 60g carb lunch, glucose steadily climbed and hovered around 185 mg/dL through mid-afternoon despite several correction doses.

events.title: Post-dinner drop
events.description: Insulin outpaced dinner carbs initially, dropping glucose to a brief low point of 88 mg/dL before the remaining food absorbed.

events.title: Late night peak
events.description: Delayed absorption from dinner carbs caused a high spike up to 213 mg/dL, keeping levels elevated well into the early morning.

events.title: Overnight recovery
events.description: Continuous micro-corrections and basal coverage successfully brought glucose back down into a steady 90–100 mg/dL range before waking.

events.title: Mid-morning rebound peak
events.description: Breakfast carbs (70g) created a delayed second wave, driving glucose up to 200 mg/dL before dropping back down by noon.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Notice how larger carbohydrate meals (dinner and breakfast) triggered delayed secondary spikes 2–3 hours later, requiring multiple correction doses.
